title: Crossing over universal scaling laws in two-dimensional driven dissipative condensates
authors: Q. Fontaine, F. Helluin, M. Escalera, D. Pinto Dias, A. Lemaître, M. Morassi, M. Wouters, A. Minguzzi, L. Canet, S. Ravets, J. Bloch
abstract: In low dimensional systems, fluctuations are enhanced and prevent the spontaneous breaking of continuous symmetries. As a result, spatial and temporal correlation functions decay at large distances and long times. A well established example is given by two-dimensional bosonic condensates at equilibrium, which do not display long-range order of the coherence but algebraic decay belonging to the Berezinski-Kosterlitz-Thouless universality class. In contrast, the universal behaviors of non-equilibrium bosonic condensates are more diverse and many open questions remain. Here, we explore the spatio-temporal coherence properties of two-dimensional driven-dissipative polariton condensates in semiconductor optical microcavities. By tuning microscopic parameters, we observe a cross-over between two scaling laws that we attribute to the Edwards-Wilkinson (EW) and the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) universality classes. We demonstrate the collapse of the measured first-order correlations onto the EW and KPZ universal scaling functions and obtain critical exponents, well matching the values predicted theoretically. Our results highlight the intrinsic non-equilibrium nature of polariton condensates and establish them as a platform of choice for controlled exploration of the two-dimensional KPZ universality class.
summary: The paper investigates universal scaling laws in 2D polariton condensates, demonstrating a crossover between the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) and Edwards-Wilkinson (EW) regimes. By measuring spatio-temporal coherence, the authors confirm that these driven-dissipative systems serve as an excellent platform for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena. This bridges fundamental statistical theory with advanced quantum optics experiments.
main_problem: The study investigates universal scaling laws, specifically the crossover between Edwards-Wilkinson (EW) and Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ), governing coherence decay in non-equilibrium systems.
main_result: The authors experimentally demonstrate that 2D polariton condensates exhibit clear crossovers between KPZ super-diffusive and EW diffusive scaling regimes by tuning system parameters. They also show that topological defects are largely paired, suggesting the underlying physics is governed by phase fluctuations at large scales.
method: The research combines experimental measurements of spatio-temporal first-order coherence with numerical simulations to analyze defect dynamics and correlation functions.
model_or_system: The physical system is two-dimensional driven-dissipative polariton condensates realized in semiconductor optical microcavities. The behavior contrasts with equilibrium 2D bosonic systems (BKT class) by exploring non-equilibrium universality classes like KPZ and EW.
key_observables: Spatio-temporal first-order coherence function ($g^{(1)}(\Delta\mathbf{r}, \Delta t)$), critical exponents, defect pair correlations ($g^{(2)}$), and vortex/anti-vortex lifetimes ($	au$).
important_parameters: System detuning ($\hbar\delta$), excitation power ratio ($p = P/P_{th}$), spatial filter width ($\sigma_f$), and interaction strength ($g_R$) relative to loss rates.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that at large scales, the coherence decay is dominated by phase fluctuations, allowing for the separation of density correlations from universal scaling laws. Numerical simulations require an energy cutoff ($	au_c$).
figures_summary: Figures show heat maps and temporal/spatial coherence decays confirming KPZ (stretched exponential) and EW (power-law) scaling at different detunings. Supplementary figures detail vortex clustering, defect lifetime distributions, and pair correlations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context by contrasting equilibrium (BKT) vs. non-equilibrium physics. It then presents experimental evidence for KPZ/EW crossovers using coherence measurements, followed by detailed numerical analysis confirming that phase fluctuations dominate over short-lived topological defects at macroscopic scales.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly controllable, solid-state platform (polaritons) to experimentally verify fundamental concepts from non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, such as the KPZ universality class, which is crucial for understanding driven many-body systems.
